cards.explanation: Paul asks, "Tell me, you who want to be under the law, do you not understand what the law says?" (Galatians 4:21). So the question is whether they understand what the law says. I think it stings a little, because he's asking about the very thing they say they want. And he's about to show them what it says, so stick with me, friends.

The answer is False. Paul says Abraham "…had two sons, one by the slave woman and the other by the free woman." (Galatians 4:22). So only one son was born to a free woman. The other mother was a slave woman, and Paul builds the whole lesson on that split.

The two blanks are flesh and promise. Paul says the son by the slave woman "…was born according to the flesh…" (Galatians 4:23). That son was Ishmael, Hagar's boy (Genesis 16:15), born after Sarai gave Hagar to her husband Abram as a wife (Genesis 16:3). The son by the free woman "…was born through the promise." (Galatians 4:23). That son was Isaac, and God had told Abraham that Sarah would bear him a son (Genesis 17:19).

The answer is Mount Sinai. Paul says, "One covenant is from Mount Sinai and bears children into slavery…" (Galatians 4:24). Sinai is the mountain this covenant comes from. Hold onto that name, friends, because Paul ties it to a woman in the very next breath.

The answer is Hagar. Paul says the covenant from Mount Sinai that bears children into slavery: "This is Hagar." (Galatians 4:24). Hagar is the slave woman from Abraham's story. Paul uses her as a picture of that covenant.

The reason is that she is in slavery with her children. Paul says Hagar corresponds to the present-day Jerusalem "…because she is in slavery with her children." (Galatians 4:25). The match is about slavery. Nothing else about the city is part of his reason.

The answer is False. Paul says, "But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother." (Galatians 4:26). Free, not in slavery. That little word "But" shows he's pointing to a different Jerusalem than the one he just talked about.

The reason is that she will have more children than the married woman. The words say, "…more are the children of the desolate woman than of her who has a husband." (Galatians 4:27). That's the reason she's told to rejoice. The children of the desolate woman are more than the children of the woman who has a husband.

The answer is Isaac. Paul says, "Now you, brothers, like Isaac, are children of promise." (Galatians 4:28). Isaac was the son born through the promise. Paul puts the Galatian believers right alongside him.

The answer is that he persecuted him. Paul says, "At that time, however, the son born by the flesh persecuted the son born by the Spirit." (Galatians 4:29). He doesn't say how or give details here. He just states that it happened.

The answer is False. After saying the son born by the flesh persecuted the son born by the Spirit, Paul adds, "It is the same now." (Galatians 4:29). So the trouble didn't stay in the past. Paul says it carries on in his own day.

The reason is that her son will never share in the inheritance. The Scripture says, "…the slave woman’s son will never share in the inheritance with the free woman’s son." (Galatians 4:30). That's the reason given. It's about the inheritance, and nothing else is added.

The answer is False. Paul ends with, "Therefore, brothers, we are not children of the slave woman, but of the free woman." (Galatians 4:31). He had just called them children of promise like Isaac (Galatians 4:28), so this is where he was heading. And he says "we," friends, so he counts himself in with them.
